blocks.text: Exciting new talent in photojournalism: the IPPG 2026 recipients – in pictures

The winner of the 2026 Ian Parry photojournalism grant, which spotlights new talent in photojournalism, is Maddie McCuddy, 23, from the US. She receives £10,000, Canon equipment and mentorship from Giles Duley (Legacy of War Foundation). Jospin Mwisha, 22, from DRC was highly commended, and Ike Wood, 23, from the US was commended. The recipient of the 2026 Save The Children x IPPG Commission is Fin J Kerr, 21, from the UK, and the recipient of 2026 Gentex Corp personal safety award is Louis Lemaire-Sicre, 23, from France. We take a look at a selection of their work

Identical triplets Allison, Amber, and Fryman, 23 at their house in Cynthiana, Kentucky, July 2026. The sisters all have cerebral palsy and have graduated from high school this past spring. Photograph: Maddie McCuddy/IPPG 2026

Verna Petidt with her 74-year-old father, Vernon, in the front yard of his property in Oddville, Kentucky, August 2026. Verna has cared for her father full-time since moving into a trailer on his property, but she plans to move within the next month to Paris, Kentucky, with the support of a section 8 housing voucher. She is unsure who will care for Vernon after she leaves as he can’t manage on his ownPhotograph: Maddie McCuddy/IPPG 2026

Vernon Petidt, 74, spends the remaining daylight with his cats on his porch, where he sleeps most nights. He has collected an abundance of stray cats, which he feedsPhotograph: Maddie McCuddy/IPPG 2026

Alicia (standing), Allison (lying), and Amber (sitting) Fryman at their house in Cynthiana, Kentucky, July 2026. The identical sisters, 23, have cerebral palsy. Having graduated from high school in the spring, they are now navigating the realities of entering womanhood as individuals, as well as the boredom that comes from the confinement of their own home owing to the lack of accessibility to care. Lisa, their mother, rarely leaves the house. ‘Sometimes before my dad gets home, my mom will walk with us to the stop sign and back on our street,’ says AliciaPhotograph: Maddie McCuddy/IPPG 2026

Amber, Alicia and Allison play basketball near their house. Although basketball is one of their favourite hobbies, they are rarely allowed to leave the house during the day to play unless Allison’s caregiver or one of their other sisters is present. Their mother takes care of them nearly full time, while their father works as a landscaper for a cemetery. Alicia says she hopes to get a ‘fancier pair’ of Nike Jordans soonPhotograph: Maddie McCuddy/IPPG 2026

Amber applies makeup before she begins livestreaming on TikTok. Most of the girls’ communication throughout the day is via texting, FaceTime, and other apps on their phonesPhotograph: Maddie McCuddy/IPPG 2026

Amber (left) and Alicia (right) watch Allison’s caretaker’s baby. Allison has gone through a few different caretakers in the past few months, while Amber and Alicia are waiting to hear back from a programme called Active Day in Lexington, an adult daycare centre. They have been on the waiting list for more than six months nowPhotograph: Maddie McCuddy/IPPG 2026

A settlement in Mongbwalu, in Ituri province, Democratic Republic of the Congo, where artisanal miners live. These makeshift shelters are located close to gold extraction sites, 16 June 2026Photograph: Jospin Mwisha/IPPG 2026

Female miners displaced by war sort gold particles at an artisanal mining site in Mongbwalu. They carefully select gold-bearing stones under precarious conditions, 16 June 2026Photograph: Jospin Mwisha/IPPG 2026

Specialists help healthcare providers don personal protective equipment before examining patients in the isolation ward during their shift at the Munigi Ebola treatment centre (ETC) near Goma, DR Congo, after it was reopened by MSF. The centre currently has five suspected cases and can accommodate up to 80 patients. 2 June 2026Photograph: Jospin Mwisha/IPPG 2026
A child returning from school stops to look at Ebola awareness illustrations displayed outside the ETC in Munigi, 2 June 2026.Photograph: Jospin Mwisha/IPPG 2026

Family and midwives weep as the body of a person who died from Ebola arrives at a cemetery in Bunia, Ituri province, 13 June 2026. The body was transported by Red Cross volunteers involved in safe and dignified burial operationsPhotograph: Jospin Mwisha/IPPG 2026

26 Federal Plaza, formerly known as the Jacob K Javits federal building, and the neighbouring Ted Weiss federal building in New York together house more than seven floors of immigration courtrooms, a labyrinth that can overwhelm immigrants with limited English proficiency as they search for the right room on the right floor at the right time. 13 November 2025Photograph: Ike Wood/IPPG 2026

Federal agents march into a crowd, spraying chemical irritants at protesters who have gathered in front of the Delaney Hall detention centre in Newark, New Jersey, to clear a path for federal vehicles, 26 May 2026Photograph: Ike Wood/IPPG 2026
ICE agents stand outside the Delaney Hall detention centre as protesters gather to voice concerns over reported conditions inside the facility, 28 May 2026Photograph: Ike Wood/IPPG 2026
A detainee fixes a cutout heart to a window and chants ‘Si se puede’, (Yes you can) along with the protesters outside the Delaney Hall detention centre, 28 May 2026Photograph: Ike Wood/IPPG 2026
An ICE agent corners a protester near a moving 18-wheel tractor-trailer, which injures the protester’s leg, outside Delaney Hall, 29 May 2026Photograph: Ike Wood/IPPG 2026

An XL Bully wearing a studded collar chews on a traffic cone in parliament square during the second Unite the Kingdom rally, 16 May 2026. The dog type was banned by the UK government in 2024, making ownership a criminal offence unless the owner gains an exemption. The dogs must be muzzled in publicPhotograph: Fin J Kerr/IPPG 2026

A woman enters the Dnipro River early in the morning for epiphany. A small group worked to clear a space wide enough at the frozen edge of the river to allow believers to plunge in. In the Orthodox tradition, immersion imitates that of Christ and absolves the faithful for the coming year. Kyiv, Ukraine, 6 January 2026Photograph: Louis Lemaire-Sicre/IPPG 2026
